ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Sterile necrosis

A 57-year-old woman has necrotizing pancreatitis. She is stable, blood cultures are negative, and evaluation finds no infected necrosis or other infection. A trainee suggests antibiotics solely because necrosis is present. Which response is most appropriate?

  1. Treat every necrotic collection as proven infection
  2. Add an antifungal solely because CT shows necrosis
  3. Avoid antibiotics even if infection later develops
  4. Do not give prophylactic antibiotics solely for sterile necrosis
  5. Give lifelong broad-spectrum antibiotics
Answer and explanation

Do not give prophylactic antibiotics solely for sterile necrosis

Pancreatic necrosis alone is not an indication for prophylactic antibiotics.

Option explanations

Do not give prophylactic antibiotics solely for sterile necrosis: Pancreatic necrosis alone is not an indication for prophylactic antibiotics.

Give lifelong broad-spectrum antibiotics: There is no indication for lifelong prophylaxis.

Treat every necrotic collection as proven infection: Necrosis can be sterile.

Add an antifungal solely because CT shows necrosis: Imaging necrosis does not establish fungal infection.

Avoid antibiotics even if infection later develops: Documented or strongly suspected infection changes management.
